sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Ohio County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
The Ohio County Sheriff's tax office collects the bills, and the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the values behind them. The tax office is at 301 South Main Street in Hartford, with a mailing address of PO Box 186, Hartford, KY 42347, and the phone is 270-298-4444.

The county's own sheriff page lists weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., plus the first and last Saturday of each month from 8:00 a.m. to noon. A 24-hour drop box sits on the tax office door, postmarked mail is accepted, and bills can be paid by cash, check, money order or card at the counter or online through the sheriff's site. The PVA, who handles address changes, homestead questions and assessment disputes, answers at 270-298-4433.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Ohio County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Ohio County covers about 596 square miles in the Western Coal Field region, which makes it the fifth-largest county in Kentucky by area. Hartford is the county seat and Beaver Dam is the largest city. The other incorporated towns are Centertown, Fordsville, McHenry and Rockport, and the Rough River crosses the county while the Green River runs along its southwestern edge.

The county was formed in 1798 and was once a major coal producer. About 76 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census, so many sales involve acreage rather than subdivision lots. Census figures give the rest of the picture.

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 23,934, up 0.7 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $121,400.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.2 percent of 9,107 households.
  • Median household income: $57,798; persons in poverty: 15.3 percent.
  • Housing units: 10,377, with only 3 building permits recorded for 2025.

sections.h2: When are Ohio County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in the fall and the payment window runs from October 1 until the April 15 hand-off to the county clerk. The sheriff's tax page publishes the following steps for Ohio County.

Ohio County property tax payment periods (Ohio County Sheriff's Office tax information page)
Payment periodWhat applies
October 1 to November 12 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount of the bill
January 1 to January 315 percent penalty
February 1 to April 1521 percent penalty bracket
After April 15Unpaid bill moves to the County Clerk

The 5 percent and 10 percent steps match KRS 134.015; the 21 percent February figure is the sheriff's published bracket, which folds in additional charges. The January 1 assessment date fixes who owes the year's bill, so a house sold in March still carries a bill in the seller's name that the closing agent must settle.

The sheriff advises anyone who has no bill by October 10 to request a duplicate, which can be mailed, faxed or emailed during the collection period.

sections.h2: What happens after April 15 in Ohio County?
sections.html:
The sheriff cannot collect prior-year taxes after April 15. Unpaid bills go to the Ohio County Clerk, who works from an office at 301 S Main St, Suite 201, in Hartford (weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) and takes recording calls at 270-298-4423. The clerk's delinquent tax page said the 2025 tax sale would be held on October 23, 2025 at 9:00 a.m., so that date has passed; ask the clerk for the date of the next one.

  • A lien is recorded against the parcel, and the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency.
  • Interest of 1 percent per month starts, along with clerk and county attorney charges, according to the Department of Revenue's collection guide.
  • Buyers at the sale who exceed three certificates in a county, five statewide or $10,000 in total must register with the state.
  • If nobody pays by sale day, an investor can purchase the lien and then charge the owner for it.

A seller with a recorded certificate should ask the clerk for a written payoff amount before the closing date, since the figure rises every month.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an Ohio County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA office, then move up one level at a time. Kentucky assesses at fair cash value as of January 1, and an owner who disagrees asks for an informal conference during the tax roll inspection period, which normally opens the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days. Bring recent comparable sales, repair estimates and photos of any damage.

If the conference does not settle it, the next step is an appeal form from the County Clerk, due one business day after the inspection period closes. A three-member local board of assessment appeals hears the case. A further appeal goes to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, which must receive it within 30 days of the mailed ruling, as described in a PVA appeal guide that explains the statewide process. During an appeal the owner may pay on the value the owner claims, with a supplemental bill following if the final value comes out higher.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Ohio County owners ask about?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is for owners who are 65 or older, or who are totally disabled, and who live in the home. The sheriff's page also points owners with a 70 percent VA rating or a 100 percent Social Security disability determination to the PVA. Approval removes a fixed dollar amount from the assessed value, and the state adjusts that amount every two years, so ask the PVA for the current figure.

The exemption follows the owner, not the house. A buyer who qualifies must file a new application. Farm tracts, which are common in a county this size, are assessed at agricultural value under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution when they meet the farm use rules, and the PVA can tell an owner whether a tract qualifies.

sections.h2: What tax costs come up when closing an Ohio County sale?
sections.html:
Three items reach the closing table: the current year's bill, any certificate of delinquency, and the state transfer tax. The transfer tax is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, charged to the seller and collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded (KRS 142.050). At the county median of $121,400, that works out to 243 units of $500, or $121.50.

  • Ask the sheriff's office whether the current-year bill is paid and by whom, since lenders often pay from escrow.
  • Ask the clerk whether any delinquent certificate or lien is recorded against the parcel.
  • Put an in-care-of address for the next tax bill into the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.

Heirs selling a parent's house should also expect the clerk to ask for the personal representative's affidavit listing who received the property.

sections.h2: What shapes the Ohio County housing market?
sections.html:
Ohio County's economy leans on retail, transportation and health care. Census figures put 2022 retail sales at about $255.6 million, or $10,876 per resident, and transportation and warehousing receipts at $58.4 million. Employer establishments numbered 371 in 2023, and total employment grew 14.3 percent from 2022 to 2023.

Workers spend a mean of 28.1 minutes getting to work. Fordsville, Rockport and McHenry are small towns, so an owner contesting a value will usually need to bring sales from beyond a single town.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Ohio County property taxes?
faqs.a: At the Ohio County Sheriff's Office, 301 South Main Street, Hartford, or by mail to PO Box 186, Hartford, KY 42347. Online payment is available through the sheriff's website, and a 24-hour drop box is on the office door.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay without penalty in Ohio County?
faqs.a: December 31 is the last day to pay the face amount. Payments from November 2 through December 31 carry neither discount nor penalty, and a 5 percent penalty starts January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Ohio County house if the tax bill is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is settled from your sale proceeds at the closing table, and the title company will request payoff figures from the sheriff or, after April 15, from the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Ohio County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Ohio County PVA at 270-298-4433. The sheriff only collects the bill and cannot change a value.

faqs.q: How much is the Kentucky transfer tax on a typical Ohio County sale?
faqs.a: About $121.50 on a home at the $121,400 county median, calculated at 50 cents for every $500 of value or fraction of $500. The seller owes it when the deed is recorded.
